mcqs.question: What does `helm rollback payments-prod 3` actually do?
options: Deletes and recreates the release from scratch
Downgrades the chart's version number in the repository
Rolls back only the Deployment resource, leaving other resources untouched
Reverts the entire set of manifests for that release back to revision 3's rendered state
mcqs.explanation: Helm tracks full release history, so a rollback reapplies the complete rendered manifest set from that earlier revision — every resource the chart manages, not just one. It doesn't touch the chart repository's published versions, and it's a revert-and-reapply, not a delete-and-recreate.

mcqs.question: Why can a Kustomize base directory be applied directly with `kubectl apply -f base/`, unlike a Helm chart's templates directory?
options: The Kustomize base is plain, valid YAML with no template placeholders, while Helm templates contain unrendered `{{ }}` syntax
Helm charts are binary files that kubectl can't read
kubectl has no built-in support for Kustomize
mcqs.explanation: Kustomize's base is ordinary Kubernetes YAML — no templating syntax — so it's valid input to kubectl on its own; overlays only add patches on top. Helm templates contain Go template placeholders that must be rendered by the Helm engine first. kubectl also has Kustomize support built in natively via `-k`.

mcqs.question: Someone runs `kubectl patch` directly against a Deployment that a Helm release manages. What's the risk the next time someone runs `helm upgrade`?
options: Nothing — Helm always detects and preserves manual patches automatically
The manual change can be silently reverted, since Helm's recorded release state doesn't know about it
The upgrade will fail outright and refuse to proceed
Helm will merge the patch permanently into the chart's template
mcqs.explanation: Helm compares against its own recorded release manifest, not the live cluster state — a manual patch outside Helm isn't reflected there, so the next upgrade can overwrite it without warning. Helm doesn't auto-detect or auto-merge out-of-band changes, and it won't refuse to proceed just because of drift.

mcqs.question: A `pre-upgrade` hook Job that runs a database migration fails. What does Helm do?
options: It runs the migration again with `--force` automatically
It skips the hook and proceeds with the upgrade anyway
It marks the release failed and stops before touching the Deployment, so new code never runs against an unmigrated schema
It rolls back to the previous release automatically
mcqs.explanation: A failed pre-upgrade hook halts the release before any resource update — the entire point is to prevent new Pods from starting against a database schema that never finished migrating. Helm doesn't auto-retry the hook, silently skip it, or auto-rollback; the release is simply left failed for a human to investigate.
